I ran `python -m pytest` once. The tool truncated about 20,000 characters from the middle of the output, so my list may be incomplete.

Test files with failures that I can see in the output:

- `tests/test_arguments.py`
- `tests/test_basic.py`
- `tests/test_commands.py`
- `tests/test_context.py`
- `tests/test_options.py`
- `tests/test_parser.py`
- `tests/test_utils/test_echo_via_pager.py`, which fails with an empty pager output where `'just text\n'` was expected.

The truncated section covers the end of the progress lines after `tests/test_utils/test__expand_args.py`, and the failure details and short summary. I can't confirm that no other files fail in that part. All the other files I could see showed no failures. The skips (`s`) and the single expected failure (`x`) don't count as failures.

The first six files are the same ones that have uncommitted modifications in git status. I haven't investigated why they fail.

I didn't re-run the suite, since you asked for a single run. To get the complete list, I can re-run it with the same command writing to a file, or with `-rf` so the summary isn't lost. Tell me if you want that.
